data.title: Navi Pillay awarded Peace Prize: 'Lifetime spent fighting for what's right & to uphold human rights'
data.description: Haxie Meyers-Belkin is pleased to welcome Rosa Freedman, Professor of Law Conflict and Global Development at the University of Reading. Navi Pillay's career represents a remarkable contribution to international law and human rights, from her pioneering role in post-apartheid South Africa to her work at the United Nations. Yet her legacy also raises difficult questions about political impartiality, particularly in relation to Israel and Gaza. She believes we need to distinguish between the significance of her lifelong achievements and the controversy surrounding the decision to award her the Nobel Peace Prize at this particular moment. More broadly, this debate invites us to examine whether the prize is recognising individual merit or increasingly serving as a vehicle for political messaging. At a time when international law and multilateral institutions face mounting pressure, and serious threats, Freedman asserts that the challenge is to scrutinise their shortcomings without undermining the principles they exist to uphold.

data.title: Angry French students take to the streets. British students don’t – and I think I know why | Kitty Sayers
data.description: I grew up in France, where all children are taught about the revolutionary roots of their nation and what the state owes its citizens. The lessons leave their mark Young British people have plenty to be angry about. Crushing student debt, private-school privilege, a housing market they can’t enter. Yet unlike their French counterparts, they have little tradition of turning that frustration into collective action. I grew up in France as a Briton, and for years I have watched my French friends do something my British ones never seem to: take to the streets. “To arms, citizens! Form your battalions! Let’s march, let’s march!” It shouldn’t be too surprising, given the rousing lyrics of La Marseillaise, that France’s revolutionary spirit is not a relic of the past. Kitty Sayers is a master’s student in journalism Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Like a drill going into my eye’: why the mystery over Havana syndrome refuses to die
data.description: Dozens of CIA officers have been afflicted by debilitating symptoms over the past decade. Are they the result of ‘mass hysteria’? Or are they from attacks with an energy weapon and, if so, who is responsible? And has there been a cover-up? Shortly after 1am one night in April 2019, a CIA officer on a work trip to London was jolted awake in his hotel room by the most intense head pain he had ever experienced. His body was soaked with sweat and he felt like his eyes were spinning in their sockets. He manoeuvred his way out of bed, hoping to make it to the bathroom to vomit, but found his sense of balance had deserted him. Eventually, he fell back into a fitful, shallow sleep. The next day, arriving at the work meeting he had travelled for, the officer found he could not remember the names of colleagues in the room, people he knew well. As the meeting got under way, he could barely follow the discussion. Initially, he chalked it up to a terrible – if rather odd – case of food poisoning. But over subsequent weeks, worrying symptoms persisted: brain fog, loss of balance and increasingly harsh tinnitus. Continue reading...

They were three weeks into an archaeological expedition of the waters around Khortytsia – a rocky island 12.5km long and 2.5km wide that lies just downstream of the city of Zaporizhzhia, in south-eastern Ukraine. High above the island, a Shahed drone whined on its way. A Ukrainian interceptor, and small-arms fire from the ground, tried, unsuccessfully, to bring it down. The archaeologists ignored it. This is life as normal, 28 miles (45km) from the combat zone in Russia’s war on Ukraine. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘People forgot I existed’: Audrey Niffenegger on taking 14 years to write a sequel to The Time Traveler’s Wife
data.description: Her debut made her a global star. Now she has finally written a follow-up – and this time, it’s political. She talks about impostor syndrome, screen adaptations and becoming radicalised The artist and novelist Audrey Niffenegger began writing the long-awaited sequel to her bestselling debut, The Time Traveler’s Wife, in 2012, just after Obama’s re-election. It was a “rosy” time in American politics, “as good as it gets over here”, she says now, but her new novel required her to imagine what the world might look like in 20, 40, 60 years’ time. In the 14 years she spent exploring various dystopian futures, American politics moved on. And her imaginings began to look worryingly realistic. An early scene in the new book involves a group of neo-Nazis at a house party. When she was writing it, few people believed the US would witness a resurgence of neo-nazism. It’s not like she is “psychic or anything”, she tells me, the clues were all there. “The first thing I remember reading in the news was Watergate, and so I’ve grown up with Reagan, and the Republicans coming on stronger and stronger, so that every Republican president we get is more of a disaster. And I thought the logical progression of that would be fascism,” she says. Continue reading...

data.title: Time: David Tennant and Siobhan Finneran are stellar in this horrifying and exceptional TV drama
data.description: Jimmy McGovern’s grab-you-by-the-throat prison show is back and it could hardly be more urgent, prescient or excellent. Brace yourself though … Bake Off it is not It takes a lot to drag me away from comfort TV in the autumn. Blame the shrinking hours of light or the apocalyptic news cycle but the closest thing I like to get to televisual trauma in October is watching comedians get into their own graves in The Celebrity Traitors. I doubt I’m alone. I don’t want to psychoanalyse the British public but I’d take a punt that collectively we are just about capable right now of looking at Josh Widdicombe trying to find a purpose next to Emma Willis on the Strictly dancefloor (and reportedly , even that’s a struggle). Enter legendary Jimmy McGovern with a new series of the Bafta-winning prison drama Time (Sunday, 9pm, BBC One) to drag the nation out of its Bake Off-related coma. Having already covered the devastation of men’s and women’s prisons in the first two series, the good news is that McGovern and co-writer Samuel Bailey’s trilogy surely can’t get any more distressing. The new episodes will be set in * checks notes* a youth offending institution for boys. OK great. It’s about children in prison. Thank you, Jimmy! I hope you’re happy! No one else is going to be. data.title: Remember Me review – narrow view of two photographic centuries is like a history of food in three ham sarnies
data.description: Bourse de Commerce, Paris There are 700 works from François Pinault’s collection on display – more than half of them by Irving Penn – but it’s a blinkered selection and annoyingly didactic ‘Beware … of assuming the sterile attitude of the spectator, for life is not a spectacle” scream the words of Aimé Césaire – writ large and bold by Barbara Kruger, in a giant installation, The History of Tears, that fills Bourse de Commerce’s spectacular Rotunda. Kruger’s angry, menacing, viscerally charged work – words as images, and large-scale video clips of people seething with self-hate – is a thrilling setup for Remember Me, an exhibition that promises a take on 200 years of photography through 700 works by more than 70 artists drawn from the collection of the French billionaire François Pinault. That excitement quickly dissipates as the exhibition moves on. This is the biggest photography show ever held at the Bourse de Commerce. Remember Me has two main problems: first, it tries to say too much with too few artists. For a start, nearly 450 of the 700 or so works are by Irving Penn. It leans heavily on classical, conventional approaches, styles and familiar names, and that creates a very obvious skew in the perception of what photography is, does, and how it is presented. Continue reading...

data.title: Stacey Dooley: ‘My skirt fell down on the Strictly Live tour. I was wearing big borrowed stage briefs‘
data.description: The broadcaster on her days as a shoplifter, catastrophising, and a first kiss with her dance partner Born in Luton, Bedfordshire, Stacey Dooley, 39, left school at 15 and worked as a shop assistant. In 2007 she was selected to take part in the BBC reality series Blood, Sweat and T-Shirts. This led to the series Stacey Dooley Investigates and her career as presenter of hard‑hitting documentaries. In 2018, her face-to-face confrontation with an Islamic State soldier won her the One World Media award and she also received the MBE for services to broadcasting. She has made three new investigative films for the BBC and presents BBC series Clickbait Clinic. She met dancer Kevin Clifton when they were partnered on Strictly Come Dancing; they have a daughter and live in Merseyside. What is the trait you most deplore in yourself? I’m quite greedy. I achieve something or something’s feeling really brilliant and I’m, like, “Right, what are we doing next? What are we getting next?” Continue reading...

data.title: Spa bliss in the Alps: hot springs and hiking in the shadow of Mont Blanc
data.description: An autumn break in the French mountain town of Saint-Gervais-Les-Bains offers thermal treatments and glorious walking trails before the winter ski crowds descend Mont Blanc is hiding behind the clouds, but the Aiguille du Midi spears the sky above a mountainside ablaze with russet, gold and tawny tones. The maples flare red; rowan trees are dusted with crimson berries. Our little group has trundled up to Mont Lachat station (altitude: 2,115 metres) on the Tramway du Mont Blanc, the century-old cog railway that climbs improbably steep slopes from the French alpine town of Saint-Gervais-les-Bains. Operational since 1909, the railway was once intended to reach the 4,809-metre summit of Mont Blanc, but war, glacial terrain and waning funds put an end to that ambition. But even from Mont Lachat, the view is a showstopper. On one side, the Bionnassay Glacier slips scenically down the slope, a buzzard soaring over the milky-green glacial lake at its base, while on the other the Chamonix valley basks in soft autumnal sunshine. Continue reading...

data.title: Andy Burnham is lucky – Polanski, Farage and Badenoch all seem determined to help him | Jonathan Freedland
data.description: Everywhere the PM turns, he finds generous adversaries. They have made his early days in No 10 so much easier I don’t know where Andy Burnham found his magic lamp, but I hope he’s taking good care of it. In the early hours of Friday morning, the genie that’s looked so kindly on him these past few months granted him yet another wish, with a byelection win in Holborn and St Pancras. It was just the latest gift for a prime minister for whom things keep going right – and who is especially blessed in his choice of opponents. Let’s start with that win in London, where Labour’s Sagal Abdi-Wali defeated the Green party leader, Zack Polanski. It’s easy to miss how rare such a victory is. As the veteran psephologist Peter Kellner pointed out, this was a win that “ defied history ”. If the past half-century were any guide, Labour should have lost, thanks to a “truly dreadful record” defending its own seats when in government and facing a byelection challenge from the left or centre-left, the likes of the Greens or the Lib Dems. The average swing against Labour in such contests had been 24%. “On those figures,” wrote Kellner, “Polanski should have won at a canter.” But he lost. Jonathan Freedland is a Guardian columnist Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.description: Fixing the broken education system will be just the start. The biggest challenge for an aloof political class is to finally pay attention to an abandoned generation When adolescents protest that the government is failing to uphold their right to an education, and the government’s response is to send in riot police, the government has lost the plot. People outside France may have spent the past week watching the student protests in Paris and other cities, and thought, “Well, France has a long tradition of insurrection” or, “That’s just the French being French.” But the situation that has provoked the high-school walkouts and teenage anger is most likely not one they would immediately associate with the France of their imaginations. In place of its lost plot, the French government has a collection of anecdotes and statistics that it should be ashamed of: 27th place in the most recent OECD education rankings , schools with ceilings collapsing and rats in classrooms and, in a school in Bagnolet, no drinkable water ; an increase in the average number of students per class from 27 in 2010 to over 30 today ; half of primary and high schools missing teachers at the start of the school year – many of them with no substitutes or replacements. Alexander Hurst writes for Guardian Europe from Paris. His memoir Generation Desperation is out now Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on the 90s revival: the end of the analogue age | Editorial
data.description: The new exhibition at Tate Britain is part of a wider cultural resurgence from 30 years ago. This is nostalgia for a pre-digital era Each generation imagines itself to be cooler than the one that went before it, and weirder than the one that comes after it, to update George Orwell. Gen X is no exception. “It felt like something was happening,” Pulp’s Jarvis Cocker writes in the catalogue for The 90s: Art and Fashion , which opened at Tate Britain this week. “Something good. It felt like the weirdos were taking over.” The exhibition, curated by the former editor of British Vogue, Edward Enninful, is part of a wider 90s cultural revival. Oasis’s Wonderwall was the UK’s unofficial World Cup anthem this summer, after last year’s sellout reunion tour . Pulp have also just completed a world tour. The 1993 novel Trainspotting has become a musical; less surprisingly, so has 90s-set romance One Day , which found a new audience with 2024’s Netflix series . Love Story , which fictionalises the doomed relationship between John F Kennedy Jr and Carolyn Bessette, broke streaming records. Cult drama This Life is now on iPlayer. Vogue has described the era as “fashion’s most revisited decade”. Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on Labour and the Greens: winning trust takes more than words | Editorial
data.description: A byelection win is a fillip for Andy Burnham and shows Zack Polanski must confront the failures damaging his party’s credibility and appeal By holding Holborn and St Pancras, Andy Burnham’s Labour has shown it can attract liberal and left-leaning voters. The seat has substantial numbers of young adults, students, professionals and Muslims – offering fertile ground for the Greens’ ecopopulism. However, Labour prevailed. Having won leave-voting Makerfield in June, Mr Burnham can now claim an appeal that bridges Labour’s divided electorate. It’s worth noting that turnout in London was low and Labour’s vote share fell 3.7 points. But that compares with an average 19.3-point fall in four byelections under Mr Burnham’s predecessor. The new leader clearly has bought Labour breathing space and checked the Green advance. The Greens more than tripled their vote share in the constituency to 33%. But they were beaten. Labour’s Sagal Abdi-Wali took 45% in Sir Keir Starmer’s former seat, leaving Zack Polanski’s ambition of entering parliament unfulfilled. For a party that began the year promising to turn voters’ hunger for change into a serious challenge to Labour, this was a sobering moment. The passing of a motion declaring “Zionism is racism” at its conference probably cost the party support – though the result in central London alone cannot definitively say that. There is a separate question of leadership. Mr Polanski now says he would have voted against the motion. Why, then, did he not make his opposition clear when it mattered last weekend? Continue reading...

data.title: After the strongest storm in a generation, Hawai’i residents take recovery into their own hands – in pictures
data.description: On Kaua‘i, neighbors repair each other’s roofs, teens deliver meals and locals use their own equipment to clear roads It was a few hours after the sun rose over the verdant valleys and clear waters of Hā‘ena on Kaua‘i’s North Shore. Michael Olanolan was already in his excavator, clearing the main highway where a wall of fallen trees had blocked access. Other neighbors joined him, moving debris so electric crews could reach utility poles downed by Hurricane Lowell. The 76-year-old father of nine and grandfather of 26 did this every day for weeks after Lowell hit the Hawaiian islands of Kaua‘i and Ni‘ihau on 7 September. His generational home lost part of its roof to Lowell’s winds, but family and friends helped him repair it, freeing him up to also help his community. Clearing out roadways became his full-time job while residents were getting back on their feet. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘They looked like two curtain-twitchers, though not very subtle ones’: Peter Crome’s best phone picture
data.description: The photographer was walking home in London when he caught the attention of a pair of canine snoops Walking home after dropping his little girl at school, Peter Crome sensed he was being watched. A former professional ballet dancer now living in London, he had supplemented his income with photography work for 20 years. “But since having my daughter, my Nikon gear has sat idly by,” he says. “I got so used to lugging my heavy equipment around with me, it’s been quite refreshing to go somewhere just with a phone and still come back with wonderful pictures. My iPhone has also been a blessing for keeping in touch with family back home in Sydney,” Crome adds. The cause of his disquiet that day was, to his happy surprise, these two dogs. “It was such a comical moment,” he says. “They looked like two curtain-twitchers, though not very subtle ones. I liked how they were perfectly framed with the different layers of window frames, and the brickwork and hedge provided some pleasing textures, but it was the disapproving expression on their faces that made the photo for me.” Continue reading...

data.title: 14th review – Ava DuVernay’s galvanizing documentary is a remarkable achievement
data.description: New York film festival: the director has made a fascinating and troubling companion piece to her Netflix documentary 13th, which takes a fiery look at American injustice It feels at once like the blink of an eye and an eternity since Ava DuVernay’s documentary 13th arrived on Netflix, a month before the election of Donald Trump to his first term as president. The intervening decade has more or less borne out the film’s thesis on the enduring specter of white supremacy in American life: that a clause within the 13th amendment abolishing chattel slavery – that involuntary servitude could be used as punishment for a crime – was immediately and continually exploited to criminalize black people, mass incarceration thus being the modern incarnation of America’s original sin. The Oscar-nominated film, which saw a surge in viewership during the protests of 2020, has remained both a time capsule of late Obama-era moral clarity and, arguably, the acclaimed director’s best picture. At least, until now – 14th, DuVernay’s sequel, of sorts, soon also to arrive on Netflix, is just as lucid and galvanizing as its predecessor, with an updated, more pressing urgency befitting a democracy in distress. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I just wasn’t going to give up’: the fight to free the longest-serving political prisoner in the US
data.description: Leonard Peltier was imprisoned for 49 years before his sentence was commuted. A new Netflix documentary exposes the ‘corrupt’ system that allowed it to happen On 20 January 2025, with 14 minutes remaining in his term as president, Joe Biden commuted the life sentence of Leonard Peltier , after years of pressure to release a figure seen by many as the longest-serving political prisoner in the US. The Indigenous activist, a leader within the American Indian Movement (Aim) and an icon of Native American resistance, served nearly 50 years in prison for allegedly killing two FBI agents during a shootout on the Pine Ridge reservation in South Dakota, in 1975 – killings he has always denied, prosecuted in a railroaded trial widely seen as corrupt. Outside the Florida prison where Peltier was being held that morning were several of the many activists and lawyers who fought for his release, as well as film-makers David France and Jesse Short Bull. The two directors’ long-gestating documentary on Peltier’s fight for justice was set to premiere just a week later at the Sundance film festival with a very different ending, the octogenarian still awaiting a chance to return home to the Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa reservation in North Dakota. That morning, there was “a sinking feeling that it wasn’t going to happen”, France said. Continue reading...

data.description: In this week’s newsletter: Dead-eyed billionaires can’t hold a candle to the maniacal cinematic villains of old – it’s time Hollywood rewrote its source code • Don’t get The Guide delivered to your inbox? Sign up here Sixteen years ago The Social Network was released and the first stirrings of a new cinema archetype were seen: the tech-bro villain. Perhaps that’s too damning a description for the Mark Zuckerberg portrayed by Jesse Eisenberg in David Fincher’s 21st-century classic about the dawn of Facebook; he’s certainly not a villain in the mwah-ha-ha, moustache-twirling sense. But he is, at the very least, on the wrong side of antiheroic: brilliant, brittle, status-craving, cruel and in charge of a social network with an exploding user base. Back then of course, the ramifications of this combination of troubling personality traits and transformative technology hadn’t quite dawned on us all: to many, social media sites still seemed a societal net positive. But the character was chilling enough to give even the most Pollyanna of tech evangelists a moment of pause. Fast forward to 2026, when faith in social media – and technology more broadly – is at Mariana Trench lows, and a sequel to Fincher’s drama has arrived in cinemas, this time both written and directed by the first film’s writer, Aaron Sorkin. The Social Reckoning whizzes the action forward to the tail end of the 2010s, by which time Facebook has grown into a near-trillion-dollar monolith. It follows real-life data engineer Frances Haugen (played by Mikey Madison), whose concerns over the radicalising qualities of Facebook’s algorithm prompt her to leak confidential files to investigative journalist Jeff Horwitz (Jeremy Allen White), resulting in the release of the Wall Street Journal’s Facebook Files . Right around the same time as this damaging publication, and also depicted in the film, is the small matter of a riot-slash-insurrection at the Capitol, egged on by the outgoing US president on, among other places, Facebook, prompting his belated ban from the platform by Zuckerberg. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I’ve hit my midlife sexpot era!’ Romola Garai on marital misery, cheating … and sex scenes in cars
data.description: Layby hookups are all in a day’s work for Romola Garai in her steamy new drama Adultery. She talks faking orgasms, keeping secrets – and making audiences pass out In a raging storm in the Peak District last winter, a blue Toyota Yaris was parked in a remote roadside spot with a sex scene being filmed inside it. “It can pose challenges, depending on the size of the car,” chuckles Romola Garai. “Me and Dominic [Cooper] got in this hatchback and asked: ‘How far do these seats go back?’ Soon there was a gale blowing outside. We were in the car, ready to shoot, but outside the entire film crew were being buffeted by high winds. They said: ‘You guys stay in there, don’t get out!’ while all the lights were getting blown away.” What did the co-stars do while the camera crew battled the elements? “What actors always do in these situations – have a long, gossipy conversation about people in the industry. While everyone else was trying to save the show, we were sitting in the car, like: ‘Well, I’ve heard he’s a total nightmare!’” Continue reading...

data.title: Stark warning – does new footage in Avengers: Endgame reveal the truth about Doctor Doom?
data.description: Warning: contains spoilers The four short scenes added to the new version has made the film the highest-grossing of all time – but the only people really enjoying this are the Disney accountants Does it really matter which film is the highest-grossing of all time at the global box office? Will James Cameron be lying awake at night staring into the darkness and pondering whether to withdraw humanity’s access to giant, blue-skinned space elves out of sheer spite, just because Avatar has been dethroned once again by Avengers: Endgame? It seems unlikely. Are the Russo brothers at this very moment leaping and capering with wild abandon because adding a few new scenes and releasing their film for the umpteenth time has led to this momentous changing of the guard? Probably not. Is a Disney accountant somewhere holding a tiny awards ceremony in which every nominee is himself? Well yes, absolutely, because the mouse house ultimately owns both films. And yet the most interesting thing about Avengers: Endgame’s return to cinemas is not how much money it has made – for the record, the rerelease, titled Avengers Endgame: Encore, had brought in another $126m worldwide by last weekend, taking its lifetime total to approximately $2.925bn (just ahead of Avatar’s $2.923bn) – but what Marvel added to the picture while we were all busy counting. data.title: ‘Sometimes she publishes notes she’s scribbled on her hand’: Édouard Louis on 10 reasons to love Anne Carson
data.description: The French author discovered Carson on a bus while stranded in a snowstorm and has been enthralled by her fearless imagination ever since Where to start with Anne Carson ‘Delights await!’: Margaret Atwood and other writers on Nobel winner Anne Carson 1. Anne Carson is one of the greatest writers of our time. I discovered her work on a Peter Pan bus from New York to New England. I’d bought Antigonick in a bookstore a few days earlier, almost randomly. From the very first lines, I was enthralled. While we were on the bus, a snowstorm suddenly blanketed the roads, and the other passengers and I found ourselves stuck for 10 hours in rural America, surrounded by an entirely white landscape. I took my computer out of my backpack and started to translate Antigonick into French. Spontaneously. I was so absorbed by the power of Carson’s text that I didn’t notice the hours pass. 2. One of Carson’s greatest strengths is that, unlike so many other contemporary writers, she doesn’t try to “make literature”. She writes. Sometimes clouds do the speaking, in her work, and sometimes monsters do; sometimes, in the middle of a collection of poems, she lets an imaginary Catherine Deneuve take over the narration. Sometimes she writes a letter to her own sleep and sometimes she publishes notes she’s scribbled on her hand. She writes about Homer, but also Rosalía; about Brecht, but also Marilyn Monroe. Translated by Josh Cohen Continue reading...

data.title: Winning the Nobel prize in literature only underlines Anne Carson’s infinite genius | Yiyun Li
data.description: When her sons died the Book of Goose author turned to Grief Lessons, Carson’s translation of four plays by Euripides. She reflects on the ‘life sustaining’ work of an extraordinary writer • Where to start with: Anne Carson • ‘Delights await!’: Margaret Atwood and other writers on Anne Carson It is preposterous to agree to write a short piece on Anne Carson’s work. The task is impossible, akin to that of solving the mathematical problem of dividing zero by zero. If one had the power to solve it, perhaps one would have some confidence in attempting to write about Anne Carson’s work. Attempting, I say, not succeeding. In attempting to do so, I shall emphasise that all words fall short in extreme situations, which not only include unfathomable losses ( of children, in my case ) but also include articulating anything about Anne Carson’s work. One could start with Carson’s words. “Words, if you let them, will do what they want to do and what they have to do.” (Autobiography of Red) But to let the words exist in their own desires and yearnings and frustrations and confusions, to let the words scream with inarticulable pain or tell a riddle with a twinkling smile or make love to one another – how many of us have achieved that kind of mastery of words? But, oh no, mastery is the wrong word here. Only the minor and the greedy and the power-thirsty writers want to be the masters of the words. Carson does not subjugate or manipulate her words. She lets them be; and lets herself be led by the words – hers, and the ancients’ translated into unforgettable English by her. Continue reading...

data.title: The best recent science fiction, fantasy and horror – review roundup
data.description: The Ballad of Black Tom by Victor LaValle; As You Wake, Break the Shell by Becky Chambers; The Eye of Goliath by Diego Muzzio; Our Cut of Salt by Deena Helm The Ballad of Black Tom by Victor LaValle ( Penguin , £9.99 ) This short novel won almost every genre award following its 2016 US publication. As a Black writer, LaValle had a conflicted relationship with the works of HP Lovecraft. As a child, he loved the tales of cosmic horror, but grew to recognise the racism and other prejudices of the author. Unable to “throw the man’s stories away” because of how formative they were on his own imagination, he decided to write his own response to one of the most obviously racist, The Horror at Red Hook, recasting it through the perspective of a musician and hustler from 1920s Harlem later known as Black Tom. It’s a powerful tale of horror – both everyday and the occult – told with sheer brilliance. As You Wake, Break the Shell by Becky Chambers ( Hodderscape, £22 ) In this cosy science fiction love story set on a distant planet, life is a constant struggle for the human colonists. As the book opens, botanist Signy is yet to meet the love of her life, Cora, a rorqual pilot. Rorquals are gigantic interplanetary creatures, trained by human pilots whose implants allow them to communicate with the beasts as they transport supplies. Chapter 1 is followed by chapter 764, set more than a decade later, when the two women are blissfully married. The non-linear narrative may reflect what we’re told is the rorqual view of time, but it also removes much suspense. The characters are adorable, and the details of growing plants in an artificial environment, or Cora’s relationship with her rorqual, are enjoyable, but readers may grow impatient with the glacial pace and reiterations of their feelings for one another. Even the “naturally solitary” rorqual is given to declaring its love for Cora. In the final pages there’s a tonal shift that ends on a cliffhanger: how Cora and Signy survive is to be revealed in a sequel. Continue reading...

data.title: 11 questions to ask yourself before going no contact with a family member

Other times it functions as an attempt to avoid grief, conflict, disappointment or the painful acceptance that a parent cannot become the person one longs for,” says Joshua Coleman, a clinical psychologist and the author of Rules of Estrangement. “Distance alone doesn’t resolve those emotions.” Continue reading...

data.title: Henry Harris’ recipe for tarte Vaudoise à la creme
data.description: This fantastic tart is a minor miracle invented by a legendary chef, yet it has very few ingredients and an intriguing technique for baking it Often, the greatest dishes are made from very few ingredients and with pretty standard techniques, and this tart is one of them. It’s based on an old Frédy Girardet recipe that, despite his reputation as one of the all-time greats, calls only for a simple application of process to deliver a knockout result (which is one reason I put it in my latest book). A pastry case is spread with sugar and cream, then dotted with butter and sprinkled with cinnamon. The pastry is not blind baked, but filled and baked in a very hot oven. That sounds wrong, but it is not: a fierce heat is needed to bake the pastry under its filling and to meld the cream, sugar and butter. A pinch of flour is mixed with the sugar and, as it all boils up, that smidgen of flour holds everything together as it bubbles and reduces until it takes on the appearance of condensed milk while the pastry cooks and toasts at the edges. I still use Girardet’s quantities because, unsurprisingly, they work perfectly. Merci , chef. Henry Harris is chef/co-owner of Bouchon Racine , London EC1. His book, The Racine Effect, is published by Quadrille at £40. To order a copy for £36, go to guardianbookshop.com Continue reading...

data.title: Send us your questions for economist Isabella Weber on inflation and affordability
data.description: First Edition newsletter will be hosting a reader Q&A with economist Isabella Weber, a leading voice on inflation, affordability and cost of living and now’s your chance to put your questions to her Isabella Weber is one of the most sought-after and influential economists of her generation, and has advised policymakers and governments in the US, Germany, Europe and Latin America. She has become a leading voice on inflation , affordability and the cost of living. Her new book, Anti-Fascist Economics, looks at the relationship between economic insecurity and the rise of the far right, arguing progressive politics must respond to the rise of authoritarianism by urgently addressing the economic pressures people experience in their daily lives. For years Weber was treated as an outlier. Weber is an associate professor of economics at the University of Massachusetts Amherst and an associate in research at Harvard’s Fairbank Center, and is the author of the prize-winning How China Escaped Shock Therapy. We’d love to hear your questions. Perhaps you would like to find out how the cost of living affects the current political landscape? What’s happening in the bond markets? Or the advice she’d give to progressive politicians, from incumbents like Burnham and Mamdani to the German parties taking on the AFD. From austerity to zero deficits, nothing is too simple or complex. Continue reading...

data.title: Ukraine war briefing: Kyiv blasts peace talks as just ‘smokescreen’ for Trump‘s Russian diesel deal
data.description: Trump’s announcement a betrayal of Ukraine, Democrats say; Ukraine strikes major datacentre in Russia. What we know on day 1,690 Ukrainian peace negotiators in Miami have been used as a “smokescreen” for a “weak” decision by Donald Trump to lift diesel sanctions on Russia , Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in a furious response to the US president’s backflip on Russian sanctions. In a move likely to create a fresh crisis with Washington’s Nato allies, Trump announced the deal with Putin on his Truth Social network, saying it was essential to reduce fuel prices in the US, which have soared as a result of his decision to go to war with Iran. The Ukrainian president, who flew to Washington last month to plead with US lawmakers to pass tougher sanctions on Russia, said in a statement on Friday that it was “unfortunately, a weak decision by strong partners”. “I believe our team is simply being used as a smokescreen. And that is certainly not fair. It is certainly not how partners should treat each other.” Negotiators for the ⁠US, Ukraine and Europe ⁠held ​six ‌hours ‌of talks ‌in Miami on Friday with the aim ‌of reaching agreement ​on ending ​the war ​in ​Ukraine , ​a ‌source ​briefed ​on the talks said. They discussed a postwar economic package for Ukraine and potential new security architecture between Europe and Russia, the source said. President Trump announced the diesel deal as his envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner were meeting with Ukrainian officials in Florida to discuss a peace plan. Trump’s announcement was a betrayal of Ukraine, the European allies and US national security, said Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer , top Democrat on the Foreign Relations Committee Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, and senior Democrat senator, Elizabeth Warren. “Enough is enough,” the senators wrote. “The President must end his war with Iran instead of funding Russia’s war machine.” A number of prominent Republicans joined Democrats on Friday to condemn Trump for lifting the diesel sanctions , including congressman Don Bacon, who said the majority of Americans supported Ukraine. “The President’s policies towards Russia and Ukraine are failures. We need moral clarity not moral ambiguity.” Ukraine struck and partly disabled a major datacentre operated by Russian technology company Yandex on Friday in the second such action in successive days. Yandex, which is heavily involved in Russia’s ​AI development, said its data centre in the Kaluga region south-west of Moscow had been struck by Ukrainian drones and partly put out of action. Ukrainian arms maker Firepoint said Kyiv had used its FP-1 one-way attack drones to mount the ⁠strike. Four Ukrainians were arrested in Vienna this week on ⁠suspicion of spying , Austrian interior minister, Gerhard Karner, said on Friday, with Ukrainska ⁠Pravda newspaper saying two ⁠of ​its team were among those detained. Three remain in custody, Karner said, declining ⁠to provide further details because the investigation was ongoing. Austrian news agency APA quoted a ⁠spokeswoman for the Ukrainian embassy in Vienna as saying ​it was awaiting ‌an explanation from the ‌Austrian authorities on the circumstances of and legal grounds ‌for the arrests. The embassy did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Russian ⁠forces struck ​three cargo vessels in and ⁠around Ukraine’s Black Sea ports on ⁠Friday , Russia’s defence ministry ​said. The ‌ministry said ‌one vessel was ‌hit in the port of Mykolaiv, another in the port of Chornomorsk and ‌a third, bound for Odesa, in the ​Black Sea. According to the ministry, all three vessels ⁠were being used ​to supply ​the Ukrainian ​military. Reuters could ​not ‌independently verify ​the ​report or the claim. Russian strikes killed three people and wounded at least eight across Ukraine, officials said Friday , as Ukraine struggles to counter escalating Russian bombardments that have killed more than 50 people over the past three days. Continue reading...

data.title: Scientists planted 40,000 seedlings in Yosemite; 3 years later, meadow is still losing carbon
data.description: Scientists planted 40,000 native sedge seedlings in Yosemite National Park's Tuolumne Meadows to restore soil damaged by sheep grazing over a century ago. After three years, researchers found improvements in soil organic matter, but the meadow continued to lose more carbon than it gained. Scientists estimate that full recovery could take 25 to 50 years.

data.title: Florida restored a degraded oyster reef in 2018; density rose to 91 per sq m in six months and 244 by year five
data.description: Florida’s Lone Cabbage Reef, once a vibrant oyster habitat, faced severe decline before restoration efforts. Researchers rebuilt the reef in 2018 using dolomite limestone to create suitable surfaces for oyster larvae. Subsequent studies documented significant increases in oyster populations over five years, reaching densities of 244 oysters per square metre. The restoration benefited local fisheries, generating substantial economic impact and employment opportunities.

data.title: Mobilisation lycéenne : à Saint-Denis, le « temps de démocratie » voulu par le gouvernement à l’épreuve de l’éveil politique des élèves

data.title: Au Texas, la Menil House, fleuron du goût de l’Amérique
data.description: A Houston, au Texas, se cache une villa singulière. Le couple de collectionneurs et philanthropes franco-américains John et Dominique de Menil y ont accueilli les plus grands artistes et intellectuels des années 1960 et 1970. La maison aux lignes épurées et à la décoration exubérante est aujourd’hui célébrée pour avoir contribué à l’émergence d’un goût authentiquement américain.

data.title: Sanctions contre la CPI : Washington lance un ultimatum aux Etats membres

data.title: Possível ministro da Saúde não consegue enxergar o negacionismo
data.description: Tem coisas que só a natureza humana faz pra você, e o autoengano certamente é uma dessas joias da coroa da evolução dos hominínios. Só mesmo tão sublime inovação cognitiva do Homo sapiens para transformar um sujeito normalmente inteligente e com elevados níveis de educação formal em alguém que fala como se tivesse esquecido o cérebro no banheiro do aeroporto. Para ilustrar esse princípio, sugiro a leitura da entrevista com o médico Claudio Lottenberg , feita por minha insigne colega Cláudia Collucci . É uma "masterclass" de autoengano. data.description: När det misstänkta övergreppet skedde för två år sedan var det inte många utanför elituniversitetet Cornell som tog notis. Men nu har nya uppgifter framkommit om en drogindränkt natt då sju män ska ha våldtagit en av skolans studenter. Polis och åklagare anklagas för en slapphänt hantering – och sociala medier brinner av det igenkännande ropet: ”Jag är den anonyma kvinnan!” Är det ett tecken på en ny Metoo-rörelse?

data.title: DN Debatt. ”Kvinnan själv vet när abort är rätt beslut – inte sex främlingar”
data.description: DN DEBATT. Inom kort ska Sverige få en uppdaterad abortlag. Men den innebär bara marginella förbättringar, kvar finns en paternalistisk och ålderdomlig syn på kvinnors självbestämmande. De i glesbygden förväntas fortfarande resa i timmar, och rätten till sen abort ligger fortsatt i händerna på sex andra personer – inte hos kvinnan själv, skriver sex medicinska experter.

data.title: Ze namen een pil tegen kaalheid en eindigden diep ongelukkig
data.description: Het begon met een paar haartjes op zijn kussen, zo’n twee jaar geleden. Erg ongerust was hij nog niet, want kaal worden leek hem „niet echt zijn stijl”. data.title: ANALÝZA: Mnichov Donalda Trumpa. Za pouhou naději u voleb obětoval spojence
data.description: Americký prezident Donald Trump šokoval transatlantické partnery, když oficiálně oznámil dohodu s vládcem Kremlu Vladimirem Putinem o okamžitém uvolnění ruské nafty pro americký a globální trh. data.title: Profesor Pafko se topil ve Vltavě. Drama popsal známý záchranář Dvořák
data.description: Uznávaný chirurg a profesor Pavel Pafko zažil minulý týden zapeklité chvíle. Vyrazil se projet Vltavou na své lodi, ta se s ním však převrhla a on zůstal uvězněný ve studené vodě. Pomalu se topil. Z vody jej nakonec vytáhli až lidé plující okolo, jeden z nich pracuje u záchranářů jako pilot vrtulníku. Příběh sdílel na svých sociálních sítích jeho kolega a známý lékař Marek Dvořák.

data.title: Bohatí ujíždějí zbytku Ameriky. Akcie jim přinesly biliony dolarů

Prohlásil to americký prezident Donald Trump, který rozhodnutí udělit ocenění jihoafrické právničce a někdejší soudkyni Mezinárodního trestního soudu (ICC) a Mezinárodního tribunálu pro Rwandu (ICTR) Navanethem "Navi" Pillayové za hanebné a trapné.

data.title: Trump žádá o prověření zamítnuté žaloby na Hillary Clintonovou
data.description: Prezident Spojených států Donald Trump požádal Nejvyšší soud USA o přezkoumání dříve zamítnuté žaloby na svou neúspěšnou demokratickou soupeřku z prezidentských voleb v roce 2016 Hillary Clintonovou. V noci na sobotu o tom informovala agentura Reuters. Republikán Trump Clintonovou, manželku bývalého demokratického prezidenta Billa Clintona, vinil ze spiknutí s někdejším šéfem Federálního úřadu pro vyšetřování (FBI) Jamesem Comeyem s cílem ovlivnit volby tím, že spojovali jeho kampaň s Ruskem.

data.title: Trump šokuje sabotováním sankcí. Nakoupí od Putina miliony tun nafty
data.description: Rusko okamžitě dodá na americký a světový trh přes 300 tisíc tun nafty, v dalších měsících pak budou následovat ještě vyšší dodávky. Oznámil to v pátek americký prezident Donald Trump na své sociální síti Truth Social. Uvedl, že dohodu o dodávkách sjednal během telefonického rozhovoru s ruským prezidentem Vladimirem Putinem, který označil za velmi úspěšný.

data.title: V zoo se narodila mláďata největších štírů světa, matka je nosí na zádech jako batoh
data.description: Návštěvníci ostravské zoo mají jedinečnou příležitost spatřit vzácná mláďata veleštíra císařského, jednoho z největších druhu štírů na světě. Samice je nosí na zádech v Pavilonu evoluce, kde si navíc lidé mohou sami vyzkoušet speciální UV lampu, pod kterou tito obří pavoukovci modrozeleně světélkují. Mláďata však v expozici pobudou jen zhruba dva až tři týdny, než se přesunou do zázemí.

data.title: Certifikát chránící děti před predátory má problém. Měnit ho chtějí nejen poslanci
data.description: K dětem by se měli od ledna dostávat hůře lidé, kteří jim někdy v minulosti ubližovali. Zajistit to má potvrzení, jímž se budou muset prokazovat ti, kteří chtějí s dětmi pracovat. Neměl by se tak opakovat třeba případ „pana Mašinky“, kdy si za znásilnění dítěte dvakrát odsouzený muž založil v Liberci spolek Děti ráje železnice. A využíval ho k sexuálnímu zneužívání a znásilňování nezletilých.

data.title: Portugal no centro do Atlântico digital. Autoestrada de dados ou potência tecnológica?
data.description: A posição geográfica de Portugal e a chegada de novas ligações submarinas colocaram o país como recetor de valor acrescentado nas rotas internacionais de dados. Operadores de telecomunicações, cabos submarinos e pontos de troca de tráfego digital concordam com o retrato. Porém, esta interdependência é sentida ainda como um princípio. Para reter valor, o país precisa de centros de dados, energia, redes terrestres, cloud, capacidade computacional e empresas que troquem e processem localmente a informação. Uma evolução a que não se pode subtrair a inteligência artificial, que aumentará a escala e a urgência deste desafio.

data.title: Rússia envia mais de 300 mil toneladas de gasóleo a todo o mundo
data.description: Os Estados Unidos acordaram com a Rússia a suspensão das sanções ao gasóleo. Moscovo oferece, em resposta, mais de 300 mil toneladas de gasóleo, numa altura em que o mundo enfrenta uma crise em matéria de abastecimento.

data.description: L’ONG Netherlands institute for multiparty democracy (NIMD) a organisé un atelier de dialogue communautaire pour le rapprochement des leaders, des élus et de leurs communautés d’origine en commune Ntahangwa de la province Bujumbura. data.title: Le mandat du Rapporteur spécial sur les droits de l’homme au Burundi renouvelé
data.description: Le Conseil des droits de l’homme des Nations Unies a renouvelé mardi 6 octobre 2026 le mandat du Rapporteur spécial sur les droits de l’homme au Burundi pour une année. Le renouvellement intervient à la veille de la présidentielle prévue pour le 03 mai 2027 au Burundi. Gitega rejette la décision.

data.title: Le PRCCB- NAGURA-ISI enclenche une révolution verte et socio-économique à Bugendana
data.description: Du repiquage de jeunes plants à Jenda au déploiement d’équipements à Bugendana, le Projet de Résilience Climatique des Collines du Burundi (PRCCB-NAGURA-ISI) a été officiellement lancé le jeudi 1ᵉʳ octobre 2026.  Quatre-vingt collines à travers 12 communes dans les 5 provinces du pays et 87 sous-bassins versants auront leurs plans de gestion et feront l'objet de travaux de restauration.

data.title: Les députés provinciaux du Kasaï-Central préoccupés par le retard des travaux de la route Kananga-Kalamba Mbuji
data.description: Le retard enregistré dans l’exécution des travaux de la route Kananga-Kalamba Mbuji continue de susciter des inquiétudes au sein de l’Assemblée provinciale du Kasaï-Central. Une délégation de députés provinciaux a échangé, jeudi 8 octobre à Kinshasa, avec les responsables de l’Agence congolaise des grands travaux (ACGT) afin de faire le point sur l’évolution de ce projet considéré comme stratégique pour l’espace Kasaï.

data.title: Maï-Ndombe : plus de 180 personnes sans-abri après l’effondrement de 45 maisons à Bolobo
data.description: Au moins 182 personnes se retrouvent sans abri depuis lundi dans le village Mokele, situé dans le territoire de Bolobo, province du Maï-Ndombe, à la suite d’une forte pluie qui s’est abattue sur la région. Les intempéries ont causé l’effondrement de 45 habitations, plongeant plusieurs familles dans une situation de grande précarité.

data.title: Le prix du sac de ciment gris fixé à 44 650 francs congolais à Kisangani
data.description: Le prix du sac de ciment gris de type 42,5 est désormais fixé à 44 650 francs congolais ( environ 20 USD) à Kisangani, dans la province de la Tshopo. Cette décision a été prise ce vendredi 9 octobre, à l’issue d’une concertation entre le gouvernement provincial et les opérateurs économiques, après une hausse des prix observée sur le marché depuis une semaine.

data.title: Beni : les cas de troubles mentaux sont passés de 1 367 à 13 282 après les premières tueries par les ADF (psychologue)
data.description: Environ 13 282 personnes souffrant de troubles mentaux ont été recensées l’année dernière dans l’ensemble du territoire de Beni, au Nord-Kivu. data.title: Ebola : plus de 300 écoles du Nord-Kivu dotées de matériels de prévention
data.description: Plus de 300 écoles primaires et secondaires de Beni, Butembo et du territoire de Lubero, au Nord-Kivu, bénéficient d’un appui en matériels de prévention contre la maladie à virus Ebola. La distribution de kits de lavage des mains et de thermomètres sans contact, fournis par l’UNICEF en partenariat avec les services provinciaux de l’Éducation et de la Santé, a débuté jeudi 8 octobre.

data.title: Joseph Kabila accuse Félix Tshisekedi de poursuivre une guerre sans perspective de victoire
data.description: L’ancien président de la République démocratique du Congo, Joseph Kabila, a critiqué la gestion de la situation sécuritaire dans l’Est du pays et dénoncé les initiatives en faveur d’un changement de la Constitution. Dans un discours partagé sur les réseaux sociaux, vendredi 9 octobre 2026, il a également mis en garde contre ce qu’il considère comme une confiance excessive du président Félix Tshisekedi dans le soutien des États-Unis, à la suite de l’accord conclu entre les deux pays sur les minerais stratégiques.

data.title: Le cycliste Joël Kyaviro déclare forfait pour le Mondial de Gravel en Australie, faute de moyens
data.description: Le cycliste congolais Joël Kyaviro ne participera pas au Championnat du monde de Gravel, prévu les 10 et 11 octobre à Nannup, en Australie. Qualifié pour cette compétition, l’athlète a annoncé son forfait ce vendredi 9 octobre, sur son compte Facebook, évoquant un manque de moyens financiers et l’absence de soutien du gouvernement pour financer son déplacement.

data.title: Bunia : les arrêtés du maire contre l’anarchie urbaine peinent à être appliqués
data.description: La ville de Bunia continue de faire face à plusieurs défis qui freinent son développement, notamment l’insécurité, la gestion des déchets, la prévention des incendies et la régulation de la circulation routière. Invité du journal de Radio Okapi vendredi 9 octobre, le maire de Bunia, le colonel Jean-Bosco Mbuyi Kola, a indiqué avoir pris plusieurs mesures pour rétablir l’ordre dans la ville. Toutefois, il regrette que certains de ses arrêtés peinent à être exécutés par la police.

data.title: Le film « Rumba Royal » choisi pour représenter la RDC aux Oscars 2027
data.description: La République démocratique du Congo a officiellement désigné le film Rumba Royal pour porter ses couleurs dans la catégorie du Meilleur film international à la 99ᵉ édition des Oscars, prévue le 14 mars 2027 au Dolby Theatre de Hollywood, à Los Angeles. L’annonce a été faite jeudi à Kinshasa lors d’une cérémonie marquée également par la présentation des membres de la DRC Film Commission et la remise du « Léopard du 7ᵉ Art », prix du Meilleur Film National, à l’œuvre sélectionnée. Selon la coordonnatrice de la DRC Film Commission, Cécilia Zoppelletto, cette étape marque l’aboutissement d’un processus lancé avec la création de la commission et l’ouverture des candidatures.

data.title: Université Mapon : 29 étudiants et deux enseignants renvoyés pour des faits de corruption avérée
data.description: L’Université Mapon a décidé d’exclure définitivement vingt-neuf étudiants et deux enseignants pour des faits de corruption qualifiés de « corruption massive avérée ». data.title: Let The Constitution direct Chieftaincy to deliver “All Development Is Local”
data.description:
Chieftaincy’s natural power and capacity to lead local development have been grossly underrated and it is time to address that constitutionally. For accelerated local development, there is an urgent need to reverse the constitutional usurpation of that local development role which it assigns to local government.

Article 245(a) of Ghana’s 1992 Constitution mandates a decentralised system of local government and administration to drive local development. So far, the article has underperformed in implementation, such that the Constitution Review Committee (CRC) seeks its review in an “all development is local” approach.

data.title: Ghana explores centre of excellence for hearing, communication and cochlear implant care
data.description:
Ghana is exploring the establishment of a Centre of Excellence for Hearing, Communication and Cochlear Implant Care to expand access to specialist hearing services and strengthen local healthcare capacity.

The proposed centre would bring together services including hearing screening, diagnosis, ear, nose and throat (ENT) care, audiology, hearing technology, cochlear implant services, speech and language therapy, rehabilitation, family support and research.

The proposal was discussed at a meeting involving Ambassador Victor Emmanuel Smith; Emilio Alonso Mendoza, president of the Alexander Graham Bell Association for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing (AG Bell); Roxana Semorile, president of Semorile Holdings, LLC; and Maabena Webb, executive director of Region17.

Participants emphasised that the proposed centre should be Ghanaian-led and complement existing health and academic institutions rather than replace them.

data.title: Schizophrenia-related disorders lead mental health cases recorded in Ghana
data.description:
Ghana’s Mental Health Authority recorded 36,196 cases involving five major mental health conditions between January and June 2026, an increase of 6,414 over the same period last year. The Authority is also calling for people with lived experience to help shape mental health policies and services.

Ghana’s Mental Health Authority (MHA) recorded 36,196 cases involving five major mental health conditions between January and June 2026, an increase of 6,414 over the same period last year.

The figures, released ahead of World Mental Health Day on October 10, compare with 29,782 cases recorded in the first half of 2025.

Schizophrenia, schizotypal and delusional disorders accounted for 15,193 cases, followed by epilepsy with 9,072 and depression with 5,939.

data.title: Dutch authorities enlist Ghana in hunt for fugitive drug lord Bolle Jos
data.description:
The Netherlands is seeking Ghana’s support to disrupt the drug supply network of fugitive Dutch trafficker Jos Leijdekkers, widely known as Bolle Jos, who is believed to be hiding in Sierra Leone.

Dutch Minister of Justice and Security David van Weel is supporting efforts to involve Ghanaian authorities in the pursuit, with the aim of cutting off supply lines linked to the fugitive’s network, according to a report by Dutch newspaper De Telegraaf.

The precise form of the support is still being worked out, but the report says it could include the deployment of Dutch police officers to Ghana.

Leijdekkers has been sentenced to more than 80 years in prison in the Netherlands and Belgium for drug trafficking and related offences. He is believed to be in Sierra Leone, where reports say he has links to influential figures, including the president’s family.

data.title: Ghana housing finance conference adopts communiqué to improve affordable housing access
data.description:
The National Conference on Housing Finance 2026 has adopted a communiqué committing government, financial institutions, housing developers, labour organisations and other stakeholders to coordinated action to improve access to affordable housing in Ghana.

The communiqué, adopted at the Mövenpick Ambassador Hotel in Accra on Thursday, October 8, outlines measures to address barriers to housing finance, promote affordable housing delivery and advance the goal of “Adequate Housing for All.”

The conference was convened by the National Housing Fund (NHF) in collaboration with public and private sector stakeholders, bringing together representatives of government, regulators, development partners, employers, academia and civil society.

data.title: Special Initiatives Minister urges Wa Technical Institute to enrol more girls as EU-backed solar training lab opens
data.description:
Minister of State in charge of Special Initiatives at the Office of the President, Abdul-Rashid Pelpuo, has urged Wa Technical Institute to increase the enrolment of girls in renewable energy programmes, saying Ghana’s transition to green technology must create opportunities for both women and men.

He made the call at the launch of a solar photovoltaic (PV) training facility at the institute, established under the EU-Ghana Pact for Skills to strengthen practical training and prepare young people for jobs in the green economy.

The €17 million initiative, implemented by the European Union, the International Labour Organization (ILO) and the Ghana TVET Service, seeks to bridge the gap between classroom instruction and practical skills development.

data.title: In the matter of my first year at the Bar
data.description:
A year ago, I heard my name read out as a member of the Bar in Ghana. Twelve months in the Court of Appeal, the High Court and the Circuit Court have since taught me more than the long years of preparation that came before. What follows is what I have learnt, written for myself and for the lawyers who will be called this Friday.

What the Rules Do Not Tell You

The rules of procedure give a court its skeleton, but the room has a living body. Judges have habits and registries have rhythms. A motion flawless on paper can still lose a day because service never reached the other side. I confirm the cause list the day before and carry spare copies. The lawyers I admire most are rarely the loudest in court. They go about their work diligently and calmly.

Moving between the High Court and the Circuit Court almost every other day has shown me they reward different instincts. The High Court wants authority and tidy bundles. The Circuit Court, particularly in family matters, sits closer to the people whose lives are in the balance, and a petitioner in a matrimonial cause wants to know when it will end.

data.title: ActionAid Ghana calls for an end to child marriage, greater investment in girls’ rights
data.description:
ActionAid Ghana has called for stronger measures to end child marriage and school-related abuse, urging government and community leaders to invest more in girls’ rights, education and leadership.

The call was made during the 2026 International Day of the Girl-Child celebration in Techiman, Bono East Region, held under the theme “End Child Marriage and Invest in Girls’ Rights.”

Addressing traditional leaders, educators, students and other stakeholders, ActionAid Ghana’s Regional Programme Manager, Kwame Afram Denkyira, said girls should be recognised as rights-holders and agents of change rather than victims in need of rescue.

data.title: Linking LEAP to productive inclusion could cut extreme poverty by 2030 – UNICEF
data.description:
The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) says linking Ghana’s Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty (LEAP) programme with the Productive Inclusion Initiative (PII) could reduce extreme poverty by 2.5 percentage points by 2030.

The organisation is urging the government to ensure that social protection laws translate into tangible support for vulnerable households.

The call was made at the launch of the Social Protection Act, 2025, and the Social Protection and Affirmative Action Regulations in Accra on October 7, 2026.

UNICEF welcomed the Act’s emphasis on coordination and complementarity, saying stronger links between social protection programmes could help address the multiple challenges facing vulnerable families.

data.title: Ghana expects economic boost as World Assemblies of God Congress brings 10,000 delegates to Accra
data.description:
Ghana is expected to benefit economically from the arrival of more than 10,000 delegates from nearly 200 countries for the World Assemblies of God Congress in Accra from October 14 to 16, 2026.

The three-day gathering will bring together pastors, ministers and church leaders from across the world, creating potential business opportunities for the hospitality, transport, tourism and food sectors, as well as local traders.

The congress will also mark the first time in its 50-year history that the global Assemblies of God gathering is being held in Africa.

Speaking on Joy FM’s A Walk With Jesus, Dr Kwadwo Boateng Bempah, Assistant Superintendent of Assemblies of God Ghana, said the global Assemblies of God fraternity had about 89 million members.

data.title: Sud de Madagascar : près de 3,7 millions de personnes menacées par une grave crise alimentaire
data.description: La situation alimentaire devient particulièrement préoccupante dans le Grand Sud de Madagascar. Alors que la période de soudure n'a pas encore commencé, plusieurs localités enregistrent déjà des cas sévères de malnutrition. Selon une enquête de l'AFP, relayée par Paris Match, près de 3,7 millions de Malgaches pourraient être confrontés à une insécurité alimentaire aiguë dans les prochains mois. Une perspective alarmante, dans un contexte marqué par la sécheresse, la hausse des prix et la (…) - Société

data.title: 18 groupes électrogènes russes pour renforcer la production de la JIRAMA
data.description: Le gouvernement accélère ses initiatives pour faire face à la crise énergétique. La JIRAMA a reçu l'ordre de procéder à l'acquisition de 18 groupes électrogènes auprès de Malmekhservice, une entreprise de droit russe. Cette opération, décidée dans le cadre de l'état d'urgence énergétique, sera réalisée sans appel d'offres. Chaque équipement devrait développer une puissance de 1 mégawatt, selon les indications d'un technicien de la compagnie nationale. Les installations permettraient ainsi (…) - Energie

data.title: Nasry Asfura envía mensaje de solidaridad a Panamá tras terremoto
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras. El presidente de Honduras, Nasry Asfura , expresó su solidaridad con el pueblo panameño tras el sismo registrado recientemente en ese país y reveló que se comunicó con su homólogo, José Raúl Mulino , para manifestarle su respaldo ante la situación. A través de una publicación en su cuenta de X, el mandatario hondureño informó que contactó a Mulino pocos minutos después de conocer lo ocurrido, con el propósito de transmitirle un mensaje de apoyo y cercanía. “Ante lo sucedido en Panamá , me comuniqué de inmediato con el presidente @JoseRaulMulino, a pocos minutos de conocer los hechos, para expresarle mi solidaridad y cercanía en estos momentos difíciles”, escribió Asfura. El gobernante también destacó los vínculos de amistad entre ambas naciones y aseguró que Honduras acompaña a Panamá ante las circunstancias que enfrenta. “Honduras acompaña a Panamá en este momento y reafirma sus lazos de hermandad y amistad”, agregó en su mensaje. Asfura concluyó su publicación con palabras de bendición para ambos países: “¡Dios bendiga Panamá! ¡Dios bendiga Honduras!”. El pronunciamiento se suma a las muestras de solidaridad expresadas desde Honduras hacia Panamá tras el movimiento telúrico.

A través de una publicación en su cuenta de X, el mandatario hondureño informó que contactó a Mulino pocos minutos después de conocer lo ocurrido, con el propósito de transmitirle un mensaje de apoyo y cercanía. “Ante lo sucedido en Panamá , me comuniqué de inmediato con el presidente @JoseRaulMulino, a pocos minutos de conocer los hechos, para expresarle mi solidaridad y cercanía en estos momentos difíciles”, escribió Asfura. El gobernante también destacó los vínculos de amistad entre ambas naciones y aseguró que Honduras acompaña a Panamá ante las circunstancias que enfrenta. “Honduras acompaña a Panamá en este momento y reafirma sus lazos de hermandad y amistad”, agregó en su mensaje. Asfura concluyó su publicación con palabras de bendición para ambos países: “¡Dios bendiga Panamá! ¡Dios bendiga Honduras!”. El pronunciamiento se suma a las muestras de solidaridad expresadas desde Honduras hacia Panamá tras el movimiento telúrico.

data.title: Copeco descarta alerta de tsunami tras fuerte terremoto en Panamá
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras. La Secretaría de Gestión de Riesgos y Contingencias Nacionales ( Copeco ) informó que ya no existe amenaza de tsunami para las costas hondureñas, tras el terremoto de magnitud 7.6 registrado este viernes en Panamá . La institución mantiene el monitoreo de las condiciones marítimas y de la actividad sísmica en la región. En un boletín informativo emitido este 9 de octubre, Copeco explicó que el sismo tuvo una profundidad preliminar de 10 kilómetros y motivó la emisión de un aviso por parte del Centro de Alerta de Tsunamis del Pacífico (PTWC), debido a la posible generación de olas que podrían afectar principalmente las costas panameñas. De acuerdo con las estimaciones citadas por la institución, a Nicaragua, Honduras y El Salvador podrían llegar olas inferiores a los 30 centímetros, cuya altura sería poco perceptible en comparación con el oleaje habitual. Copeco señaló que se descartó la alerta para las costas hondureñas. No obstante, indicó que mantendrá la vigilancia ante posibles actualizaciones de los organismos especializados. La institución también advirtió que continúa dando seguimiento a los reportes técnicos sobre el comportamiento del mar y la actividad sísmica en la región, incluida la posible ocurrencia de réplicas que podrían motivar nuevas evaluaciones del riesgo. Ante esta situación, las autoridades recomendaron a la población mantenerse informada mediante los canales oficiales y evitar compartir datos no confirmados que puedan generar alarma. Copeco indicó que cualquier cambio en las condiciones de amenaza será comunicado oportunamente por las autoridades competentes. Aunque las estimaciones divulgadas apuntan a olas de poca altura para Honduras, las autoridades recomiendan a las personas que se encuentren en zonas costeras tomar las medidas de precaución.

data.title: Un terremoto de magnitud 7,6 sacude Panamá
data.description: Ciudad de Panamá, Panamá. Un terremoto de magnitud 7,6 sacudió este viernes el sureste de Panamá, con una profundidad de 10 kilómetros, informó el Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos (USGS). De acuerdo con el reporte del USGS, el epicentro se registró cerca de la localidad de Tonosí, ubicada en el suroeste de Panamá, y a unos 239 kilómetros de la capital, Ciudad de Panamá. El movimiento ocurrió a las 12:56 hora local (17:56 GMT), y fue reportado inicialmente con una magnitud de 7,6, que luego fue actualizada a 7,7 por el USGS. El temblor se sintió con fuerza en algunas zonas de la Ciudad de Panamá , donde varios edificios en la antigua área bancaria fueron desalojados preventivamente, como constató EFE. En los últimos meses, en Latinoamérica se han presentado terremotos de gran magnitud. En Venezuela, ocurrieron los primeros dos sismos, seguidos uno del otro, de magnitud 7,2 y 7,5, el pasado 24 de junio, generando destrucción masiva en La Guaira , a unos 30 kilómetros de Caracas . Según el último informe del Gobierno venezolano ofrecido el pasado 24 de agosto, los sismos dejaron al menos 6.509 muertos, 14.239 viviendas con afectaciones moderadas y 11.001 viviendas con daños graves. En Colombia, la mañana del 10 de agosto un terremoto de 7,4 afectó a 500 municipios de 16 departamentos, la mitad de los 32 que tiene el país, donde 486.917 personas pertenecientes a 303.934 familias sufrieron algún tipo de afectación. Las autoridades colombianas han cifrado los muertos en 335, así como en 4.516 los heridos.

data.title: Papa León XIV recibe a obispos hondureños y envía un importante mensaje a Honduras
data.description: Ciudad del Vaticano, Italia. El papa León XIV llamó a la Iglesia católica a fortalecer la defensa de la dignidad humana y fomentar una cultura de paz en la nación hondureña, durante un encuentro con los nueve obispos de la Conferencia Episcopal de Honduras (CEH) , celebrado este viernes en el Palacio Apostólico del Vaticano. La reunión se desarrolló como parte de la visita Ad Limina Apostolorum , durante la cual los obispos compartieron con el pontífice las principales preocupaciones, esperanzas y desafíos que enfrenta la población hondureña. Monseñor Jenry Ruiz, obispo de Trujillo, Colón, relató a Vatican News que el Santo Padre insistió en la importancia de respetar la dignidad de todas las personas, sin distinción por su condición, y de promover los principios de la doctrina social de la Iglesia, especialmente la justicia y la defensa del bien común. Según Ruiz, el papa también animó a los obispos a trabajar por una sociedad menos marcada por la violencia, mediante iniciativas que impulsen el diálogo, la reconciliación y el respeto entre los hondureños. El obispo explicó que ese compromiso debe comenzar en las familias, las escuelas y las comunidades, con una formación que ayude a cada ciudadano a contribuir a una convivencia más fraterna. En ese contexto, destacó la necesidad de que la educación para la paz se convierta en una tarea compartida por toda la sociedad. “Es necesario que cada hondureño se convierta en un educador para la paz”, expresó monseñor Ruiz al reflexionar sobre el mensaje del pontífice. El encuentro, que inicialmente estaba previsto para durar una hora, se prolongó por más de dos horas. Durante ese tiempo, León XIV escuchó a los representantes de la Iglesia hondureña y conoció de primera mano las situaciones que generan preocupación entre los fieles y las comunidades del país. La reunión también estuvo marcada por el fallecimiento de monseñor Teodoro Gómez , obispo de Choluteca y vicepresidente de la Conferencia Episcopal de Honduras, quien murió el 28 de septiembre. El papa León XIV expresó sus condolencias a la Iglesia hondureña por la muerte del prelado, cuyos restos fueron sepultados el jueves anterior. Su fallecimiento ocurrió pocos días antes de la visita de los obispos a Roma. Como parte de las actividades en el Vaticano, los miembros de la Conferencia Episcopal de Honduras también visitaron los Jardines Vaticanos, donde cantaron a la Virgen de Suyapa, patrona de Honduras, en una expresión de fe y devoción por el pueblo hondureño.

data.title: Herramientas contra la ansiedad: ¿cómo bajar el volumen de una mente ruidosa?
data.description: SAN PEDRO SULA. La ansiedad puede aparecer de forma inesperada: antes de una exposición en clase, durante una reunión de trabajo, al no recibir un mensaje de la persona que te gusta, o incluso mientras estás sentado tranquilamente en casa. Aunque suele sentirse como una enemiga, en realidad es una respuesta natural del organismo ante situaciones que interpreta como amenaza. Desde el punto de vista científico, la ansiedad involucra una interacción entre el cerebro, el sistema nervioso y las respuestas hormonales del organismo. Ante una situación percibida como peligrosa, el cuerpo puede aumentar la frecuencia cardíaca, la respiración y el estado de alerta para prepararse para actuar. Esta reacción puede ser útil ante un peligro real, pero cuando aparece sin una amenaza evidente hay que investigar más a fondo las causas que pueden variar en cada persona según su contexto. La Organización Mundial  (OMS) de la Salud señala que los trastornos de ansiedad se caracterizan por miedo o preocupación excesivos y pueden afectar el funcionamiento diario. En este sentido, la psicóloga Gina Soto explica que “la  frontera  entre  experimentar  ansiedad  cotidiana  y  padecer  un  trastorno  clínico  radica  en  la intensidad,  la  frecuencia,  la  persistencia  y  la  interferencia  en  la  calidad  de  vida. Según el  manual  diagnóstico  DSM-5-TR,  los  trastornos  de  ansiedad  abarcan  condiciones  como  el  trastorno  de  ansiedad  generalizada,  la  agorafobia,  las  fobias  específicas,  el  trastorno  de pánico y el trastorno de ansiedad social”. Las primeras señales físicas de ansiedad pueden ser sudoración, nervios, ganas de vomitar, temblores, escalofríos, ganas de llorar, falta de apetito, etc. También es importante reconocer que la ansiedad no siempre se presenta como una persona visiblemente preocupada. Puede manifestarse mediante pensamientos constantes, irritabilidad, dificultad para concentrarse, sensación de peligro, tensión muscular, problemas para dormir o molestias gastrointestinales. En algunos casos también aparecen palpitaciones, sensación de falta de aire o mareos. Reconocer estas señales es importante porque permite actuar antes de que la ansiedad aumente.   La experta aclara que sentir  ansiedad  en  momentos  puntuales  no  implica  padecer  un  trastorno. “La  verdadera  señal  de  alerta  surge  cuando  la  preocupación  constante  limita  las  decisiones, fomenta  conductas  de  evitación  o  altera  significativamente  el  rendimiento  social,  laboral  o personal”, señala Soto . La psicóloga explica que las personas deben aprender a identificar  las  señales  tempranas:  pensamientos  de preocupación,  tensión  muscular,  aceleración  del  corazón,  respiración  rápida,  inquietud  o necesidad  de  escapar. “Resultan sumamente  útiles  la  respiración  diafragmática  lenta,  el  anclaje  al  presente  y  la reevaluación cognitiva de las  sensaciones  físicas  para  evitar  interpretarlas  como  un  peligro inminente. También  es  importante  trabajar con los pensamientos, no anticiparse a lo peor y buscar una respuesta reflexiva”, sugiere. Es importante saber que el manejo de la  ansiedad no basta con hacer algo en el momento que nos ataca de repente, sino también  depende  de los hábitos que ayudan a  mantener regulado nuestro organismo. Para ello, la licenciada Soto indica que, entre los hábitos cotidianos más relevantes destacan: la regulación de los ciclos de sueño y alimentación, la actividad física regular, la práctica de mindfulness o relajación, el mantenimiento de una red de apoyo social y una adecuada gestión del tiempo. “La actividad física regular puede contribuir a disminuir síntomas de ansiedad y favorecer el bienestar general. No tiene que tratarse necesariamente de ejercicio intenso". "Caminar, bailar, practicar un deporte o realizar una actividad física que resulte agradable también puede formar parte de una rutina saludable. Es crucial tener en cuenta que las actividades de autocuidado no sustituyen la psicoterapia cuando existe un trastorno establecido. Si los síntomas son persistentes o incapacitantes, la evaluación por parte de un especialista resulta indispensable”, recomienda. La terapeuta concluye con un mensaje reflexivo:“Debemos  recordar que pedir ayuda profesional no significa que la persona  sea débil ni que hay  fracasado en su autocontrol. Los  trastornos de  ansiedad son condiciones de salud mental tratables y cuentan con intervenciones psicológicas y psiquiátricas eficaces”.

data.title: Conductor ebrio atropella a motociclista y trata de huir en San Pedro Sula
data.description: San Pedro Sula, Cortés. Un hombre de 36 años fue capturado este viernes luego de atropellar a un motociclista y chocar contra otro vehículo estacionado en el barrio Medina de San Pedro Sula, Cortés. Según la Dirección Nacional de Vialidad y Transporte (DNVT), el conductor dio positivo en la prueba de alcoholemia . El subinspector Luis Soto, de la DNVT en la zona norte, informó que el motociclista resultó gravemente herido y fue trasladado de emergencia al Hospital Mario Catarino Rivas , donde se reportaron fracturas en uno de sus brazos y una de sus piernas. De acuerdo con el informe preliminar, después de atropellar al joven, el conductor impactó contra otro vehículo que estaba estacionado en la 13 avenida del barrio Medina. Posteriormente, intentó huir del lugar en un taxi, pero fue capturado por agentes de Tránsito. Soto explicó que el detenido fue trasladado a las instalaciones de la DNVT para realizarle la prueba de alcoholemia , cuyo resultado fue positivo, con un registro de 173 miligramos de alcohol por cada 100 mililitros de sangre, según lo informado por el funcionario. El subinspector indicó que el hombre manifestó que había estado departiendo desde el día anterior. Por conducir bajo los efectos del alcohol, también se le aplicará la sanción administrativa correspondiente, que, según Soto, equivale a una multa de un salario mínimo, conforme a la Ley de Tránsito. La DNVT informó que el detenido será remitido al Ministerio Público para que se determine su situación legal por los presuntos delitos de lesiones, conducción temeraria y omisión del deber de socorro, según lo señalado por Soto.
